scenes.tts: Cut the right half of the spinal cord, at the tenth thoracic segment. That is a hemisection at T 10. What is lost, and on which side? The answer depends on where two pathways cross the midline. Touch and pain enter through the same dorsal root. Then they part company.

scenes.visual: The question on screen, then two lanes, touch and pain, leave one dorsal root on the patient's right side.
scenes.narration: Cut the right half of the spinal cord, at the tenth thoracic segment. That is a hemisection at T10. What is lost, and on which side? The answer depends on where two pathways cross the midline. Touch and pain enter through the same dorsal root. Then they part company.

scenes.tts: Fine touch, vibration and position sense travel by the dorsal column medial lemniscus pathway. The first axon enters the cord and climbs on the same side, in the dorsal column. It does not synapse on the way. It synapses in the gracile or cuneate nucleus, in the caudal medulla. Axons from there cross the midline and climb to the thalamus, which relays to the cortex. This pathway crosses in the medulla.
scenes.visual: A signal runs along the blue touch lane on the right side, passes the cord without a synapse, stops at the medulla nucleus, crosses the midline to the left thalamus and cortex.
scenes.narration: Fine touch, vibration and position sense travel by the dorsal column medial lemniscus pathway. The first axon enters the cord and climbs on the same side, in the dorsal column. It does not synapse on the way. It synapses in the gracile or cuneate nucleus, in the caudal medulla. Axons from there cross the midline and climb to the thalamus, which relays to the cortex. This pathway crosses in the medulla.

scenes.tts: Pain and temperature travel by the spinothalamic pathway. The first axon synapses in the dorsal horn, near where it entered. The second axon crosses the midline within a segment or two, through the anterior white commissure. Then it climbs the opposite side of the cord to the thalamus. This pathway crosses in the spinal cord.
scenes.visual: The orange pain lane on the right side synapses in the dorsal horn, crosses the midline in the cord, and climbs the left side to the thalamus.
scenes.narration: Pain and temperature travel by the spinothalamic pathway. The first axon synapses in the dorsal horn, near where it entered. The second axon crosses the midline within a segment or two, through the anterior white commissure. Then it climbs the opposite side of the cord to the thalamus. This pathway crosses in the spinal cord.

scenes.tts: Now make the cut, in the right half of the cord. Touch fibres from the right side of the body have not crossed yet. They climb in the right dorsal column, so the cut severs them. Pain fibres from the left side of the body have already crossed. They climb in the right anterolateral cord, so the cut severs those too.
scenes.visual: A red cut falls across the right half of the cord; the right touch lane and the left pain lane both run into it and stop.
scenes.narration: Now make the cut, in the right half of the cord. Touch fibres from the right side of the body have not crossed yet. They climb in the right dorsal column, so the cut severs them. Pain fibres from the left side of the body have already crossed. They climb in the right anterolateral cord, so the cut severs those too.

scenes.tts: So fine touch, vibration and position sense are lost on the right, below T 10. Pain and temperature are lost on the left. That loss begins a little lower, from about T 11 to T 12 down. Some fibres cross above the cut and escape it. Weakness is on the right as well. The corticospinal tract crossed in the caudal medulla, so in the cord it serves its own side.

Some fibres cross above the cut and escape it. Weakness is on the right as well. The corticospinal tract crossed in the caudal medulla, so in the cord it serves its own side.

scenes.tts: Touch and strength are lost on one side, and pain on the other. That is the Brown Séquard pattern. Both pathways are major routes, not the whole of touch or pain processing. Where each one crosses lets you locate a lesion. Fine touch crosses in the medulla. Pain crosses in the spinal cord.
